left_observation.process: an on-call engineer handing off an active production incident to the next on-call engineer at shift change
left_observation.pain: the incoming engineer re-diagnoses steps the outgoing engineer already ruled out
left_observation.current_carrier: a verbal handoff call between the two engineers
left_observation.failure_mode: decisions already made during the incident are repeated or contradicted by the next engineer

right_observation.process: a nurse handing off a ward patient's pending care tasks to the nurse starting the next shift
right_observation.pain: the incoming nurse re-asks the family questions the previous nurse already resolved
right_observation.current_carrier: a spoken bedside report between the two nurses
right_observation.failure_mode: care decisions already agreed with the patient are forgotten or redone by the next shift

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: capture and transfer the incident's decision log (what was checked, ruled out, and concluded) from outgoing to incoming on-call engineer
inputs: hypotheses already tested and their results (ruled out vs confirmed)
outputs: a shared, referenceable record of ruled-out and confirmed diagnostic steps for the incoming engineer to act on
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: verbal handoff call between outgoing and incoming on-call engineer
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the verbal call carries the decision record only as spoken narrative with no persistent, checkable artifact; details are lossy/reordered/forgotten in transmission or recall, so the incoming engineer cannot verify what was already ruled out and re-derives or contradicts those conclusions
left_mechanism_profile.repair: require a written, timestamped log of ruled-out hypotheses and their evidence (append-only during the incident) that the incoming engineer must read/reference as part of the handoff, instead of relying solely on verbal recounting

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: capture and transfer patient-family care-decision agreements from one shift's nurse to the next
inputs: care decisions agreed with patient/family by outgoing nurse
outputs: incoming nurse's shared understanding of already-resolved questions and agreed decisions
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: spoken bedside handoff report between two nurses
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the agreed care decisions exist only in the outgoing nurse's spoken recollection during a single verbal handoff; if that item is omitted, misremembered, or not retained by the incoming nurse, no record of the resolved decision persists anywhere the incoming nurse can check, so she re-asks the family and potentially redoes or reverses what was already agreed
right_mechanism_profile.repair: add a persistent, checkable record of patient/family care decisions already agreed (created at the time of agreement) that the incoming nurse consults, instead of relying solely on what is spoken and retained in the single handoff conversation

left_observation.process: an MRO shop supplying a wear part for an aircraft-on-ground repair
left_observation.pain: the shop holds no stock of the part beyond the average monthly draw
left_observation.current_carrier: a purchase order raised only after the part is requested
left_observation.failure_mode: when demand exceeds the average, the part is sourced by paid emergency air freight from another region

right_observation.process: a regional distribution center fulfilling retail store replenishment orders
right_observation.pain: the center holds inventory sized to average weekly sell-through only
right_observation.current_carrier: a replenishment order triggered by the prior week's actual sales
right_observation.failure_mode: when a store's sales spike above average, the shortfall is covered by paid next-day courier shipments from a distant hub

reasons: counterfactual fails: TP-02-L->TP-02-R: The proposed change resizes the shop's own held stock to a service-level buffer, but the failure mechanism is in the distribution center's replenishment carrier, which sizes orders to store-level average weekly sell-through with no variance buffer. The failure occurs upstream of any shop-level inventory policy: it is the DC's replenishment order sizing to stores that lacks the buffer, not a downstream shop's held-stock sizing. Buffering the shop's own stock does nothing to change how the carrier computes replenishment order quantities, so above-average draws would still exceed on-hand/incoming stock at the DC-to-store link and still require the paid expedite.; TP-02-R->TP-02-L: The proposed change sizes buffer off store-level demand variability for a retail replenishment order-quantity calculation; the failure occurs in an MRO/aircraft-parts carrier process that sizes stock to the mean of historical draw with reactive procurement. These are different processes with different mechanisms (retail store replenishment vs. carrier-held MRO spare stocking), so the change as described does not touch the failure's actual system.

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: guarantee an emergency-repair-priority spare of this wear part is physically present at the shop before an AOG request occurs, even when draw in a given period exceeds the historical average
inputs: historical monthly draw / usage rate for the part
outputs: part issued to the repair immediately from on-hand stock
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: reorder/replenishment policy driving stock level to the average monthly draw, triggered by a purchase order raised only after the part is requested
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier sizes on-hand stock to the mean of historical draw and only initiates procurement reactively after a request arrives; any draw above that average has no buffer to absorb it, so the shortfall must be closed by an emergency air-freight transfer from another region at the moment of need
left_mechanism_profile.repair: size the shop's held stock to cover demand above the average (e.g., to a service-level buffer or observed peak draw, not the mean), so the part is on hand before the PO/request cycle would otherwise be triggered

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: pre-position store inventory sized to expected demand variability, not just average sell-through
inputs: prior week's actual store sales (single-period observation)
outputs: replenishment order quantity
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: weekly-actual-sales-triggered replenishment order using average sell-through sizing
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the replenishment carrier sizes orders to average weekly sell-through with no buffer for demand variance, so any store-week sales draw above that average exceeds on-hand/incoming stock and the resulting shortfall must be closed by an out-of-band paid expedite (next-day courier) instead of being absorbed by planned inventory or standard replenishment lead time
right_mechanism_profile.repair: add a safety-stock/buffer sizing term (driven by store-level demand variability, not just the mean) to the replenishment order quantity calculation, so above-average sales weeks are covered by on-hand buffer instead of triggering an expedite

left_observation.process: releasing an outbound wire transfer requested near the end of the banking day
left_observation.pain: the beneficiary account details are keyed once and sent without a second person checking them
left_observation.current_carrier: the single operator who receives and enters the wire instruction
left_observation.failure_mode: funds are sent to a mistyped or fraudulent account and the error surfaces only when the intended recipient reports non-receipt days later

right_observation.process: pouring concrete for a structural slab on a schedule-pressured site
right_observation.pain: the rebar placement is checked by the same crew that installed it, with no independent hold point before the pour
right_observation.current_carrier: the installing crew's own visual check
right_observation.failure_mode: rebar is out of position or missing in a section and the defect surfaces only when a later structural inspection cores the slab

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: independent verification of beneficiary account details before an outbound wire is released
inputs: beneficiary account details as keyed by the operator
outputs: executed outbound wire transfer
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: the single operator who receives and enters the wire instruction
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier both enters and releases the beneficiary account details with no second party checking them before funds move, so a mistyping or fraudulent substitution passes through unchallenged and is only discovered after the fact when the intended recipient reports non-receipt
left_mechanism_profile.repair: require independent confirmation of the beneficiary account details by a second person before the wire is released

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: provide an independent, pre-pour verification that as-installed rebar matches the design/placement spec, catching mislocated or missing bar before it is sealed into the pour
inputs: as-installed rebar in the formed section
a checker with authority/incentive independent of the installing crew
outputs: a documented hold-point sign-off (pass/fail) gating the pour release for that section
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: the installing crew's own visual self-check performed in place of an independent hold-point inspection
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the verification function is carried by the same party whose performance is being verified, so the crew's self-interest in staying on schedule conflicts with the incentive to report their own placement errors; the check is structurally unable to surface a defect it would itself be blamed for, so the concrete is poured over the error and the mismatch is undetectable until a later, independent structural inspection cores the slab
right_mechanism_profile.repair: insert an independent third-party (or separately-accountable) hold-point inspection of rebar placement, occurring after installation and before pour release, performed by someone with no stake in the installing crew's schedule or performance record

left_observation.process: finalizing a flight's weight-and-balance calculation before dispatch release
left_observation.pain: dispatch is asked to release the flight before cargo loading is complete
left_observation.current_carrier: the load sheet, which can only be completed once loading finishes
left_observation.failure_mode: the release is delayed or reworked because the final loaded weight needed for the calculation does not exist yet at the time it is requested

right_observation.process: a hospital admitting team deciding on a new medication for an incoming patient
right_observation.pain: the admitting team is asked to prescribe before the patient's allergy history arrives
right_observation.current_carrier: a paper allergy record held at the patient's regular clinic
right_observation.failure_mode: the prescription is delayed or reworked because the allergy history, though already recorded elsewhere, was never requested or sent to the admitting team

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: provide the final loaded (actual) aircraft weight and balance figures at the moment dispatch requests the weight-and-balance calculation
outputs: final loaded weight figure available for weight-and-balance calculation
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the load sheet can only be completed once loading finishes, but dispatch requests the final loaded weight for release before loading is complete, so the value the calculation needs does not yet exist at request time, forcing a delay or rework of the release
left_mechanism_profile.repair: give dispatch a source that supplies the final loaded weight at or before the moment loading finishes (e.g. the load sheet completes/becomes available immediately upon last item loaded), so the weight-and-balance calculation never requests a value before it exists

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: surface a patient's existing allergy record to the clinician deciding on medication at admission
inputs: request/query to the clinic holding the allergy record
outputs: allergy history available to the admitting team before prescribing
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: paper allergy record held at the patient's regular clinic
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the allergy record exists and is accurate at the clinic, but nothing in the admitting process triggers a request for it, so the admitting team makes the prescribing decision with no allergy record present at all
right_mechanism_profile.repair: add a mandatory step in the admitting workflow that requests the patient's allergy record from their clinic of record before the prescribing decision is finalized

left_observation.process: running the automated test suite in continuous integration
left_observation.pain: tests fail intermittently depending on which other tests ran before them
left_observation.current_carrier: a shared in-memory database fixture reused across test cases
left_observation.failure_mode: one test's leftover state causes a later, unrelated test to assert against the wrong value

right_observation.process: stamping sheet-metal brackets on a production line using a dedicated jig
right_observation.pain: an increasing fraction of brackets fail dimensional inspection as a production run continues
right_observation.current_carrier: the stamping jig's locating pins, unchanged since the run began
right_observation.failure_mode: the jig's locating pins wear during the run, so later brackets drift out of tolerance while early brackets in the same run passed

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: isolate each test case's data so one test cannot observe another test's writes
inputs: prior test's uncommitted or committed writes
outputs: query/assertion result read by the later test
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: shared in-memory database fixture reused across test cases
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the fixture is instantiated once and reused across test cases without resetting or scoping its state between them, so writes from one test remain visible to a later, unrelated test; that test then reads state it never wrote, and its assertion checks the leftover value instead of the value it produced
left_mechanism_profile.repair: give each test case its own isolated database state (fresh instance or transaction-rollback per test) instead of reusing one shared instance across the suite

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: hold the sheet-metal blank in a fixed, repeatable position against the die so each stamped bracket's dimensions match the die geometry
outputs: consistently positioned blank per cycle
dimensionally in-tolerance stamped bracket
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the locating pins physically wear (abrade/deform) as repeated stamping cycles accumulate, progressively changing their effective geometry so the blank is positioned less accurately each cycle; positioning error grows monotonically with cycle count, producing an increasing fraction of out-of-tolerance brackets as the run progresses
right_mechanism_profile.repair: give the locating pins wear resistance (or wear compensation) sufficient to hold positioning accuracy across a full run's cycle count — e.g. harden/coat the pin contact surfaces or make them replaceable/adjustable on a schedule shorter than the drift-inducing cycle count — without changing the jig's nominal locating geometry

left_observation.process: clearing an imported container through customs at the destination port
left_observation.pain: the container sits at the port past its free time and starts accruing charges
left_observation.current_carrier: the customs entry paperwork, which is only started after the vessel arrives
left_observation.failure_mode: clearance is delayed because the required import documentation was not prepared in advance, and the delay is billed as demurrage

right_observation.process: obtaining a municipal inspection sign-off before covering a completed foundation
right_observation.pain: the crew sits idle waiting for the inspection to happen
right_observation.failure_mode: the sign-off is delayed because the inspection department has more requests that week than it has inspectors, regardless of how early the contractor requested it

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: prepare and file import customs entry documentation before vessel arrival so cargo can be released within free time
inputs: bill of lading and commercial invoice
outputs: filed customs entry
cleared container available for pickup within free time
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier's documentation-preparation step is only triggered after vessel arrival instead of during the pre-arrival window, so the customs entry filing starts too late to complete clearance before free time expires, converting the filing delay into billed demurrage
left_mechanism_profile.repair: start preparing and filing the import customs entry documentation during the pre-arrival window (upon receipt of vessel ETA/shipping documents) instead of waiting for vessel arrival

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: convert a completed-foundation state into an authorized-to-cover state via municipal inspector attestation
inputs: inspection request submitted to municipal department
outputs: sign-off / authorization to cover foundation
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the queue's service rate (inspectors available) is fixed while arriving inspection requests that week exceed it, so every request queues regardless of how early it was filed; early submission affects queue position, not queue throughput
right_mechanism_profile.repair: add inspection capacity (or an alternate authorized inspector/pathway) sufficient to clear the weekly request volume within the crew's idle-avoiding window

left_observation.process: serving product prices from a read-through cache in front of the pricing database
left_observation.pain: customers occasionally see a price that is already out of date
left_observation.current_carrier: cache entries that are not touched when the underlying price is updated
left_observation.failure_mode: a price update in the database does not trigger removal of the old cached value, so the stale price is served until it expires on its own

right_observation.process: displaying same-day revenue on an internal analytics dashboard
right_observation.pain: viewers occasionally see a number that is already out of date
right_observation.current_carrier: a nightly batch job that recalculates the dashboard's figures once per day
right_observation.failure_mode: same-day transactions are not reflected until the next scheduled batch run, so the dashboard lags true activity by up to a day even though the pipeline is working exactly as designed

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: invalidate cached price entry when the underlying price value changes
inputs: price update event/write to pricing database
cache key/entry for that product's price
outputs: cached value marked invalid or removed
subsequent reads bypass stale cache entry and refetch from database
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: cache entries (read-through cache in front of the pricing database)
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the price update path writes to the database but has no corresponding step that removes or invalidates the matching cache entry, so the old cached price remains servable until it separately expires via TTL
left_mechanism_profile.repair: on price update, invalidate (delete or overwrite) the corresponding cache entry as part of the update transaction/path

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: provide dashboard revenue figures that reflect same-day transactions as they occur
inputs: transaction/revenue events occurring throughout the current day
outputs: displayed same-day revenue figure on the dashboard
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier only recomputes and publishes the figure once per day, so any transaction occurring after the last batch run is structurally excluded from the displayed number until the next run, producing a staleness window of up to ~24 hours even though the batch job completes successfully every time
right_mechanism_profile.repair: increase the recalculation/refresh frequency of the same-day figure (e.g. intraday incremental updates) so the display window is no longer bounded by a once-per-day batch cycle

left_observation.process: coordinating framing completion with the start of electrical rough-in on a renovation
left_observation.pain: electrical work has started late on some floors
left_observation.current_carrier: a text message the framing lead sends when he believes his crew is done
left_observation.failure_mode: on two floors the text was sent before framing was actually complete, so electricians began work in areas that still needed framing changes; site management has floated requiring a walkthrough sign-off instead of a text, but this has not been tried yet and nobody has assessed whether a walkthrough would actually have caught the two incidents

right_observation.process: coordinating diagnostic completion with the start of a repair step on a multi-step overhaul
right_observation.pain: repair work has started before diagnostics were finished on some jobs
right_observation.current_carrier: a shared whiteboard mark the diagnostic technician updates when a step is believed finished
right_observation.failure_mode: on a few jobs the whiteboard was marked before diagnostics were actually complete, so repair started on the wrong assumption; a supervisor has suggested replacing the whiteboard mark with a signed checklist, but nobody has reviewed the incident records closely enough to say whether a signed checklist would have prevented those specific cases

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: gate that admits electricians into a floor only after framing changes on that floor are physically complete
inputs: actual framing completion state per floor
framing lead's belief about completion state
outputs: go/no-go signal to electrical crew to begin rough-in on a floor
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: text message from framing lead stating his crew is done
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier transmits the framing lead's belief that framing is complete, with no independent check against the physical state of the floor; on two floors that belief was wrong, so the signal reached electricians while framing changes were still outstanding and nothing in the current process could catch the mismatch before work started
left_mechanism_profile.repair: before electrical rough-in starts on a floor, add a second party's independent confirmation (e.g. a brief walkthrough) that verifies framing is actually complete on that specific floor, rather than relying solely on the framing lead's self-report

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: gate repair start on confirmed-complete diagnostics
right_mechanism_profile.inputs: diagnostic step completion state per job
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: shared whiteboard mark toggled by the diagnostic technician
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the whiteboard mark records the technician's belief that diagnostics are finished, not a verified fact, so it can be set (and read by the repair step as go-ahead) before diagnostics are actually complete, with nothing checking the claim against actual completion
right_mechanism_profile.repair: before repair may start, require confirmation that the diagnostic step is genuinely complete (e.g. a completed checklist of the required diagnostic items) rather than a single unverified status mark -- but whether a signed checklist specifically would have caught these particular cases has not been confirmed against the incident records, so this repair is provisional pending that review

right_observation.process: extending trade credit terms to a customer segment at account opening
right_observation.pain: the same customer segment keeps going delinquent a few weeks after each collections cleanup
right_observation.current_carrier: a standard credit-term offer applied to the segment regardless of the segment's typical cash conversion cycle
right_observation.failure_mode: the credit term extended exceeds the segment's actual payment capacity, so the same delinquency recurs on a repeating cycle

reasons: counterfactual fails: TP-10-L->TP-10-R: The proposed change adds a minimum-rating check at parts-desk substitution time -- an eligibility/quality gate on which part can be selected. The credit failure is caused by term sizing not matching the segment's payment capacity, i.e. a mis-sized parameter set at account opening, not a substandard 'part' being swapped in. There is no analogous minimum-rating/capacity check being added to the credit term assignment process; the mechanism generating recurring delinquency (fixed generic term exceeding segment cash conversion cycle) is untouched by this change.; TP-10-R->TP-10-L: The proposed change caps credit terms based on payment capacity (a financial/credit-risk control on account opening). The failure is a mechanical/parts-supply issue: the parts desk substitutes a component qualified only on fit, not load/wear rating, causing premature failure at the repair site. These are unrelated domains and mechanisms — capping credit exposure does nothing to change how parts are selected or rated at the parts desk, so the repair-cycle failure would continue exactly as before.

left_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: keep the component's wear rate within the original manufacturer's rated tolerance for the mounting position
inputs: replacement part selected from parts desk stock
outputs: installed part physically fits mount
part meets or exceeds OEM wear-tolerance rating for that position
left_mechanism_profile.carrier: the on-hand substitute part used for the repair
left_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the parts desk stocks/selects a part qualified only on fit-to-mount, not on load/wear rating; the substitute meets the mounting spec but is rated below the original tolerance, so it degrades and fails on a shortened cycle under the same operating load that the original design tolerance was set to survive
left_mechanism_profile.repair: at selection time, require the replacement part to meet or exceed the OEM tolerance rating for that position, not just mounting compatibility -- i.e. add a minimum-rating check to the parts-desk substitution rule, not a redesign of the mount or the machine

right_mechanism_profile.hidden_function: size the credit term offered to a customer's cash conversion cycle so scheduled payment falls within the customer's available liquidity
inputs: segment's typical cash conversion cycle / payment capacity
outputs: credit term assigned at account opening
right_mechanism_profile.carrier: standard credit-term offer applied uniformly to the segment regardless of the segment's typical cash conversion cycle
right_mechanism_profile.failure_mechanism: the carrier issues a fixed credit term sized to a generic offer rather than to the segment's actual payment capacity; when the term exceeds what the segment's cash conversion cycle can support, the customer is structurally unable to pay on time, so delinquency recurs each cycle regardless of collections cleanup
right_mechanism_profile.repair: cap the credit term extended at account opening to the segment's known cash conversion cycle (payment capacity), rather than applying the standard offer uninformed by that capacity
